segs.text: Module six A, objective one. Concentrations after multiple oral doses. Extravascular means outside a blood vessel, here by mouth, so each dose is absorbed before it reaches the plasma, and the level rises to a peak and then falls. F, the bioavailability, is the fraction of the dose, D zero, that reaches the circulation; k a is the absorption rate constant and k the elimination rate constant. The peak comes at t max, when the absorption rate has fallen to equal the elimination rate, and C max is the level at that time, so t max is found before C max. She said, max for an oral dose, you have to find t max before you can find C max.

card.m: oral: absorbed first → rise to a peak, then fall
F (no units); k<sub>a</sub> and k in hr<sup>−1</sup>
peak: absorption rate = elimination rate → t<sub>max</sub> first
IV bolus peak = C<sub>0</sub>, no t<sub>max</sub>

segs.text: The single dose line from Module five is C p equals P, times e to the minus k t minus e to the minus k a t. P, the first dose prefactor, F k a D zero over V D times k a minus k, is in milligrams per liter, the same for every dose, and neither C zero nor the peak. t max equals one over k a minus k, times the natural log of k a over k. It holds only k and k a, so a larger dose does not move it. e to the minus k t follows elimination and falls slowly; e to the minus k a t follows the unabsorbed drug and falls fast, because k a is larger.

card.m: C<sub>p</sub> = P (e<sup>−kt</sup> − e<sup>−k<sub>a</sub>t</sup>)
P = {{frac:F k<sub>a</sub> D<sub>0</sub>|V<sub>D</sub>(k<sub>a</sub> − k)}} (mg/L)
t<sub>max</sub> = {{frac:1|k<sub>a</sub> − k}} ln({{frac:k<sub>a</sub>|k}})
no D<sub>0</sub>: dose larger, t<sub>max</sub> unchanged
e<sup>−kt</sup>: elimination, slow; e<sup>−k<sub>a</sub>t</sup>: unabsorbed drug, fast

segs.text: Repeated oral doses add the same way as bolus doses: each dose adds its own curve to what is left of the earlier ones, so the levels climb to a steady state. The time to get there depends on the half life alone, so with a ten hour half life it is thirty to fifty hours. At steady state the peak is expected to be higher, because drug from earlier doses is still in the body. It also comes earlier: the peak is where absorption into the plasma has fallen to equal elimination, and at steady state elimination starts each interval already high, from the trough, so the two rates become equal sooner. She said, that t max is going to decrease.

card.m: each dose adds its curve to the leftover → climb → steady state
time to steady state: t<sub>½</sub> alone; 10 hr → 30 to 50 hr
C<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> expected > first-dose C<sub>max</sub>: drug accumulated
t<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> < t<sub>max</sub>: elimination already high at the trough → absorption rate = elimination rate sooner

segs.text: In symbols, repeated doses add two accumulation factors, with tau the dosing interval, the time between doses: r k equals one over one minus e to the minus k tau, and r a is the same with k a in place of k. e to the minus k tau is the fraction of a dose left one interval later, so one minus it is less than one and both factors are at least one. A longer tau leaves a smaller fraction, so it makes both factors smaller.

card.m: r<sub>k</sub> = {{frac:1|1 − e<sup>−kτ</sup>}}; r<sub>a</sub> = {{frac:1|1 − e<sup>−k<sub>a</sub>τ</sup>}}
e<sup>−kτ</sup>: fraction left after τ; r at least 1; τ longer → r smaller
steady state, t after the latest dose: C<sub>p</sub><sup>∞</sup> = P (r<sub>k</sub>e<sup>−kt</sup> − r<sub>a</sub>e<sup>−k<sub>a</sub>t</sup>)
before steady state, n doses: {{frac:1 − e<sup>−nkτ</sup>|1 − e<sup>−kτ</sup>}}, same with k<sub>a</sub>; n large → r

segs.text: t max at steady state is the single dose t max with one more fraction inside the log, one minus e to the minus k tau over one minus e to the minus k a tau. Since k a is larger than k, the bottom is the larger, so the fraction is less than one and t max at steady state is shorter than the first dose t max. It holds tau, so a new interval means a new t max at steady state, while a new dose changes neither t max.

card.m: t<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> = {{frac:1|k<sub>a</sub> − k}} ln[{{frac:k<sub>a</sub>|k}} × {{frac:1 − e<sup>−kτ</sup>|1 − e<sup>−k<sub>a</sub>τ</sup>}}]
k<sub>a</sub> > k → correction < 1 → t<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> < t<sub>max</sub>
depends on k, k<sub>a</sub>, τ; not on D<sub>0</sub>

segs.text: C max at steady state equals F D zero over V D, the absorbed dose spread through the volume of distribution, times r k for drug left from earlier doses, times e to the minus k t max at steady state. F and t max mark this as the oral line; without them it is the repeated bolus peak. C min at steady state is P times r k times e to the minus k tau, read at the end of the interval, starting from P, not F D zero over V D. C average at steady state is F D zero over Cl T tau, Cl T being the total clearance, with no t max and no accumulation factor.

card.m: C<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> = {{frac:F D<sub>0</sub>|V<sub>D</sub>}} × r<sub>k</sub> × e<sup>−kt<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup></sup>
F and t<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup>: the oral line; bolus: {{frac:D<sub>0</sub>|V<sub>D</sub>}} × r<sub>k</sub>
C<sub>min</sub><sup>∞</sup> = P × r<sub>k</sub> × e<sup>−kτ</sup> (P, not {{frac:F D<sub>0</sub>|V<sub>D</sub>}})
C<sub>avg</sub><sup>∞</sup> = {{frac:F D<sub>0</sub>|Cl<sub>T</sub>τ}} = {{frac:F D<sub>0</sub>|V<sub>D</sub>kτ}}

segs.text: Her Example one: a seventy five kilogram man takes two hundred fifty milligrams of tetracycline by mouth every eight hours, with F about seventy five percent, V D one point five liters per kilogram, a half life of about ten hours and k a zero point nine per hour. She asks the first dose peak, then the steady state peak, trough and average. Converted, k is zero point zero six nine three per hour and V D one hundred twelve point five liters; the first dose t max is three point zero nine hours, written three point one. P is one point eight zero six milligrams per liter, and the first dose peak is one point three five milligrams per liter, below P, because P multiplies a bracket below one.

card.m: 75 kg; 250 mg every 8 hr; F 75%, V<sub>D</sub> 1.5 L/kg, t<sub>½</sub> 10 hr, k<sub>a</sub> 0.9 hr<sup>−1</sup>

segs.text: For steady state, eight hours is less than one ten hour half life, so about fifty seven percent of each dose is still in the body when the next dose is given, and r k, one over one minus zero point five seven four, is two point three five. Almost nothing is left unabsorbed after eight hours, so r a is one. t max at steady state is two point zero six hours, about an hour earlier than after the first dose. The steady state peak is three point four zero milligrams per liter.

The steady state trough is two point four four milligrams per liter, and the average, the absorbed dose over the volume cleared in one interval, is three point zero one milligrams per liter. The pattern checks: the steady state peak is higher than the first dose peak and comes earlier, and even the trough is above the first dose peak. The average is an average over time, not the midpoint of peak and trough: here it is above the midpoint, two point nine two milligrams per liter, while for her repeated I V bolus example it was below the midpoint.

card.m: her spoken 3.3; inputs give 3.40 (3.39 with t<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> = 2.1 hr)

segs.text: Her traps are about which line to use: the steady state peak needs t max at steady state, not the first dose t max, and the trough line starts from P, the first dose prefactor, not from F D zero over V D. A quiz item asks when the steady state maximum occurs; the key, two point six hours, uses only k, k a and tau, not F, V D, the dose or the weight. Another asks what a larger oral dose changes: a higher steady state C max, not a later t max.

card.m: oral line: F and t<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup>; not {{frac:D<sub>0</sub>|V<sub>D</sub>}} × r<sub>k</sub>
C<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> with t<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> 2.06 hr, not 3.09 hr; C<sub>min</sub><sup>∞</sup> from P
750 mg every 8 hr, t½ 5 hr, absorption t½ 1.5 hr: tmax∞ = 2.6 hr; F, VD, dose, weight unused
dose larger → C<sub>max</sub><sup>∞</sup> higher; t<sub>max</sub> unchanged
